question.problem:
$\,$ $P(x):$ $x=0$ $\,$ $Q(x):$ ${x}^{2}=x$

Consider the predicates $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ above. Which of the following expresses the conditional predicate $P(x)⇒Q(x)?$

- Whenever $x=0,$ then ${x}^{2}=x$
- ${x}^{2}=x$ whenever $x=0$
- $x=0,$ provided that ${x}^{2}=x$
question.worked_solution:
Given that the implication $P⇒Q$ is true, we have the following:

- Whenever $P,$ then $Q$

- $Q$ whenever $P$

- $Q,$ provided that $P$

With that in mind, let's examine the given options.

- Option I reads

$$
\text{Whenever}\,{{x=0\text{,}}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}\,\text{then}\,{{{x}^{2}=x}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}
$$

which corresponds to $P(x)⇒Q(x).$ $\,✓$

- Option II reads

$$
{{{x}^{2}=x}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}\,\text{whenever}\,{{x=0}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}
$$

which corresponds to $P(x)⇒Q(x).$ $\,✓$

- Option III reads

$$
{{x=0\text{,}}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}\,\text{provided that}\,{{{x}^{2}=x}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}
$$

which corresponds to $Q(x)⇒P(x).$ $\,\times $

Therefore, the correct answer is "I  and II only."
